steps.label: open the Tiles tab with the site kit
steps.goal: the site kit is the architectural set -- floor, wall, corner -- and it has NO tiles at all yet, which is why the solver has nothing to place
do: press 3
steps.recovery: if the palette shows fridges and beds you are on the furniture kit: restart with `cargo run -p emerge-mapper . untitled_map --kit site`

steps.label: start the floor tile
steps.goal: a floor tile is the default cell a solver fills space with -- open on all four sides
do: press N for a new tile
steps.recovery: if nothing changes you are not on the Tiles tab: press 3 first

steps.label: build and save the floor tile
steps.goal: the open cell. Every layout is mostly this one, so it is the one worth getting right first.
do: walk the library to site/floor
press Enter
press Cmd+S
steps.recovery: site/floor is 1.00 x 1.00, exactly one cell, so the size line should read 1 x 1 with nothing under it

steps.label: start the wall tile
steps.goal: one solid side is what makes a room a room
do: press N for a new tile
steps.recovery: if nothing changes you are not on the Tiles tab: press 3 first

steps.label: build and save the wall tile
steps.goal: floor plus one wall, flush to a side. The wall has to TOUCH the boundary or the edge derives as open and the solver will happily put a doorway through it.
do: bring site/floor in with Enter
press Escape, walk to site/wall, press Enter
hold shift and press an arrow to put it flush against one side
press Cmd+S
steps.recovery: site/wall is 0.10 x 1.00; flush it lands at 0.45 off centre and still fits one cell. If the size line grows, the line under it names the piece

steps.label: start the corner tile
steps.goal: a corner is where two solid sides meet -- without it the solver can only make corridors
do: press N for a new tile
steps.recovery: if nothing changes you are not on the Tiles tab: press 3 first

steps.label: build and save the corner tile
steps.goal: floor plus two walls meeting at 90 degrees. Turn the second one with R before flushing it.
do: build the wall tile again: floor, then a flushed wall
bring a second site/wall in and press R to turn it a quarter
shift-arrow it flush against an adjacent side
press Cmd+S
steps.recovery: if the turned wall makes the tile too big, it is off centre on the axis it now spans -- plain arrows bring it back

steps.label: start the low wall tile
steps.goal: a knee-high divider reads as separation without becoming a corridor
do: press N for a new tile
steps.recovery: if nothing changes you are not on the Tiles tab: press 3 first

steps.label: build and save the low wall tile
steps.goal: floor plus site/wall_low, flush. Same shape as the wall tile but see-over, which gives the solver a way to divide space without blocking sight.
do: floor, then site/wall_low
shift-arrow it flush against a side
press Cmd+S
steps.recovery: site/wall_low is 0.20 x 1.00 and fits the same way the wall does

steps.label: do these four make a room
steps.goal: the last question no checkpoint can answer, and the only one that decides whether this kit is worth extending
do: go to the Map tab with 1
try filling a region from the composed tiles
say whether what comes out looks like architecture
steps.recovery: there is nothing to recover here -- an answer of no is the finding, and names the tile that is missing
